reason: H0 only calls plist_from_bin or plist_from_xml and then plist_free; parsing does not exercise S1's new comparison and containment APIs with independently controlled comparison values and sizes. This is material because plist_data_val_contains reaches the HAVE_MEMMEM-dependent fallback memmem, whose rolling-hash update reads *(haystack_+needle_len) even on the final loop iteration, where that expression is one byte beyond haystack_len when no earlier match returns.
evidence: fuzz/bplist_fuzzer.cc invokes only plist_from_bin(data, size, &root_node) and plist_free(root_node).
fuzz/xplist_fuzzer.cc invokes only plist_from_xml(data, size, &root_node) and plist_free(root_node).
plist_data_val_contains passes data->buff, data->length, cmpval, and fuzz-relevant n to memmem.
The fallback is compiled under #ifndef HAVE_MEMMEM, creating a configuration-specific path absent from H0's protocol.
In memmem, last is haystack_+(haystack_len - needle_len + 1); the loop includes haystack_ == last-1 and then executes hay_hash += *(haystack_+needle_len), which addresses haystack_[haystack_len].

plist_data_val_compare and plist_data_val_compare_with_size use caller-controlled n for length checks followed by memcmp, while the string/key variants use strcmp, strncmp, and strstr on caller-supplied values; none is called by H0.
recommended_action: Add a structure-aware fuzz target that parses or constructs nodes of every relevant plist type, derives separate comparison buffers, lengths, numeric values, and node-type selections from the fuzz input, and invokes all new comparison/containment APIs. Run it in configurations both with and without HAVE_MEMMEM, with focused coverage for zero-length needles, haystack_len equal to or just above needle_len, absent matches, oversized n, wrong node types, floating-point edge values, and date boundaries.
